example.setup: Illustrative later Act 1 state: repeated output pushes and a deferred repair leave the conveyor vulnerable. Stiletto restarts it, believing the director values recovery over delay. An accident injures workers and damages the line. Her self-confidence falls and stress rises. Witch is now available to inspect it.
example.note: These are authored causal examples, not a running simulation or guaranteed responses to dialogue options. Each shows one plausible interpretation; a different relationship history can produce another.

cases.name: Blame without changing pressure
cases.short: “This is your failure. Recover the quota.”
cases.belief: “I will be punished for an accident and for stopping. I must prove I can recover.”
cases.desire: Restore standing and avoid another humiliating failure.
cases.intention: Recover output before admitting further uncertainty.
cases.action: Rush a restart or withhold an ambiguous warning, if her plan and access allow it.
cases.echo: Reduced reporting leaves others with weaker information. If damage remains, renewed pressure can cause another accident.
cases.trace: The cause is remembered blame plus unchanged demands, her interpretation and the remaining hazard—not an automatic loyalty penalty.

cases.name: Reassure and fund a safer restart
cases.short: “You still have my trust. Hold for Witch’s inspection.”
cases.belief: “The director will support a pause when there is evidence of danger.”
cases.desire: Recover competence without repeating the harm.
cases.intention: Wait for verification, then restore production within the new limit.
cases.action: Report the warning and hold the restart; the player accepts downtime and provides repair capacity.
cases.echo: Reporting can improve and self-confidence recover through successful work. Later punishment for the promised pause would undermine this learning.
cases.trace: Words, stop authority and committed engineering time agree. Reassurance alone neither removes the hazard nor guarantees the plan.

cases.name: Turn the incident against a colleague
cases.short: “Back my account that Limen caused the delay.”
cases.belief: “My protection depends on supporting the director’s version.”
cases.desire: Keep the director’s support while avoiding responsibility.
cases.intention: Advance the preferred account to the people whose backing matters.
cases.action: Deliver a selective report if she accepts the bargain; refusal remains possible under other beliefs and loyalties.
cases.echo: Recipients may accept, reject or relay it. Limen can learn who blamed him; the coalition changes while the original damage remains.
cases.trace: Log the bargain, her actual belief and chosen statement separately. Acceptance is an example outcome, not a dialogue command that overrides agency.

compact: Load, wear, staffing and interventions produce output, risk and physical damage.
Perception, BDI, stress and relationship memory produce concrete plans and actions.
Messages travel through available contacts; evidence and credibility govern belief and relay. No message automatically updates the whole factory.
boundaries: Plan choice uses the supervisor’s beliefs. Execution uses the actual world: a believed-safe restart can fail. An outcome does not automatically reveal its true cause to the supervisor.
The game may permit modeled disobedience or sabotage. A command passing engine validation means it is a supported, physically possible action—not that it obeys the director or safety policy.
Preserve what was done and said, who received it, and each character’s interpretation. Later promises, accusations and reporting behaviour refer to that history.
Choose whether, when and to whom to report, and what to omit or distort. Receipt, belief, relay and stress response are distinct outcomes.

Evidence can contradict a report. Personality and trust can influence revision, but there must be defined ways to question and correct beliefs. Do not use unlimited recursive guesses about everyone’s mind.

determinism.contract: Given the same initial state, game rules, ordered inputs and recorded random draws, replay must produce the same actions and outcomes. Seeded accident variation is compatible with this; surprise to the player does not require an untraceable cause.
determinism.randomness: Keep incident randomness separate from narration and visual variation. A different caption, image choice or model-call timing must not reroll an accident. Safety affects both exposure and the possible consequences; exact distributions come later.
determinism.model: An LLM can propose a contextual interpretation, conversational act or plan at a meaningful decision point. Validate and save that proposal before it affects behaviour. Routine BDI deliberation, action resolution and propagation run without waiting on the model.
determinism.honesty: A fresh live model call is not guaranteed to reproduce the same output. Replay therefore consumes the recorded accepted model input, rather than calling the model again. If we require identical outcomes from seed and player choices alone, outcome-affecting model inputs must be fixed in advance or excluded.
determinism.fallback: At a defined decision boundary, accept a valid timely proposal or use a deterministic fallback. Record which input was used; a late answer must not rewrite an already resolved shift.
log: What this supervisor actually observed or was told
Beliefs and active concerns before the decision
Relevant stress, self-confidence and relationship memories
Intention adopted, retained or abandoned and its rule-based reason
Attempted action, actual result and any random draw
Messages sent, their audiences and subsequent belief changes
determinism.reason: The explanation must come from the inputs and decision rules recorded when the action was selected. LLM prose can express that trace; it cannot invent a plausible motive afterward.

bdi.art: Resolve the event and its viewpoint before choosing an image. Match supervisor, room, action and supported visible state. A damaged conveyor plate must not imply casualties that never occurred; a thought or propaganda image must be presented as someone’s interpretation. Reuse neutral room and character art when no exact event plate fits.
bdi.readability: Keep player evidence narrower than the author’s causal log. Warnings, stoppages, hesitation, complaints, changed reports and remembered promises make agency legible in Act 1. Brain 2.0 reveals an accumulated inner history, not retroactively invented motives.
checks: Can a safety path finish Act 1 with no accident and a different cost?
Can the same order produce a different plan for a documented difference in belief or history?
Can a supervisor make a harmful mistake while loyal, and refuse a harmful order without becoming a traitor?
Does changing the private response affect later conduct without rewriting the accident?
Can disclosure reach only some audiences, and can an attempted rumour fail?
Can repeated reassurance fail when the director’s actions contradict it?
Does a recorded run replay identically without fresh model calls?
Can every displayed event image and narrated motive be justified by the recorded event or viewpoint?

references.title: Jason BDI tutorial
references.text: BDI separates beliefs, desired states and commitments pursued through plans. This supplies the conceptual vocabulary; Loopforge’s stress, accident and relationship rules remain our design.

references.title: Jason belief annotations
references.text: Beliefs can retain whether they came from perception, communication or the agent itself. This is a useful precedent for preserving sources; it does not choose our credibility or rumour rules.

episodes.title: Episodes worth watching and inspecting
episodes.intro: A shift changes the factory. An episode follows a conflict across shifts until a commitment, relationship or operating arrangement changes. BDI decisions supply the causes; the episode view makes the collision understandable.
episodes.northStar: Produce episodes that surprise us — and explain why they happened.
episodes.collision: The Attack on Titan reference sets a standard for character collisions: strong loyalties, incompatible duties, consequential initiative and revelations that change how earlier choices are understood. Loopforge should earn that intensity through its own factory and people. The collision is prepared by decisions; no character is assigned a betrayal just to complete a dramatic beat.
contract: The same problem draws a recognisable response from each supervisor. Show it in what they notice, attempt, omit and remember, as well as their voice.
A confrontation changes capacity, authority, information or a relationship. Its residue affects a later decision; an argument that leaves nothing behind is weak material.
A surprising action has a trace back to the actor’s knowledge, competing concerns and prior commitments. The explanation must survive inspection.
episodes.exampleNote: Authored later Act 1 specimen, after Witch has introduced engineering. The sequence depends on actual choices, contacts and subsequent unlocks. It does not prescribe an accident, argument or replacement in every run; no early repair capability is implied.

beats.name: A mandate with two meanings
beats.caption: Original conveyor confrontation: procedural and production priorities. This plate does not establish an accident.
beats.condition: The quota presses while the conveyor shows warning signs. The player authorizes a faster restart and defers the repair.
beats.minds: Stiletto hears that recovery earns trust. Limen believes a stop procedure is being overridden. Both think they are protecting the factory.
beats.action: Stiletto resumes production; Limen records an objection if his reporting plan calls for it.
beats.change: A precedent about whose judgment counts enters their memories. The equipment retains the unresolved hazard.
beats.next: The risk comes from the hazard and operating choice. A sustained safe stop can take this run away from the accident path.
beats.trace: Player authorization → Stiletto’s perceived mandate → restart attempt; Limen’s witnessed override → objection. Store physical wear separately from either account.

beats.name: The accident
beats.caption: Lattice Forge room reference. No event-specific casualty image is claimed here.
beats.condition: The unresolved hazard is exposed during operation. A recorded random draw within the current risk conditions resolves an accident.
beats.minds: Stiletto sees her restart followed by harm and doubts her judgment. Workers on the line witness the consequences; other rooms do not automatically know.
beats.action: The line loses capacity. Available response plans handle rescue, stoppage and repair requests; exact plans remain to be designed.
beats.change: Workers or equipment are damaged. Stiletto’s stress and self-confidence change. Witnesses retain their own experience.
beats.next: The missing capacity makes the quota harder. Repair needs and absences create opportunities for information to travel.
beats.trace: Prior exposure + resolved incident draw → actual damage → local observations → separate belief and stress updates. Severity never comes from the selected artwork.

beats.name: Private support and public silence
beats.caption: Stiletto character reference. The proposed private exchange is described in the trace.
beats.condition: In the daily briefing, Stiletto argues that output recovery remains the priority. The player reassures her and accepts that proposal. Wider disclosure is restricted.
beats.minds: In this version she concludes that the director protects her while output recovers. The director’s intention and her interpretation remain separate.
beats.action: She commits to recovering the batch and gives a selective report. Witch receives the repair request because the machinery needs work.
beats.change: Support reduces some self-doubt, yet pressure remains. A private obligation and a limited public account now coexist.
beats.next: Witch’s repair judgment can obstruct the very recovery Stiletto believes she owes the director.
beats.trace: Consultation wording + prior history → accepted belief revision → recovery intention → attributed statement to named recipients. Record that reassurance did not repair the line.

beats.name: The repair becomes an accusation
beats.caption: Rivet Witch character reference. Her exact repair and the accusation require recorded actions.
beats.condition: Witch’s inspection finds work that requires downtime. The earlier damage and the present stoppage both contribute to lost output.
beats.minds: Witch believes an open fault must be closed. Stiletto sees her recovery promise becoming impossible. Limen may treat the stoppage as evidence that his objection was justified.
beats.action: Witch holds the line if her plan and authority allow it. Stiletto can attribute the delay to Witch in a report that another supervisor actually receives.
beats.change: Technical responsibility and public blame diverge. Backing or challenging the accusation changes credibility and willingness to cooperate.
beats.next: The repair can succeed while the working relationship deteriorates. An honest finding has become material for a self-protective account.
beats.trace: Inspection evidence → repair intention → actual stoppage; Stiletto’s threatened commitment → selective attribution. The player’s response is another event, not the official truth.

beats.name: A healthier floor looks less disciplined
beats.caption: Original Thrum conveyor gathering: visible relief with attention diverted from production.
beats.condition: Later, once Thrum is available, unresolved strain or accident news leaves an affected crew stressed. The player gives him productive time for relief.
beats.minds: Thrum regards recovery as necessary. Limen sees discipline weakening; Stiletto sees another missed production window. Cathexis may gain an audience if these workers have contact with her.
beats.action: Thrum’s intervention lowers worker stress at its established cost. Other supervisors choose whether to object, cooperate or carry their criticism into a report.
beats.change: Workers can feel better while authority becomes more contested. Relief does not decide whose account of the accident is true.
beats.next: A low output ranking can now penalize the person preventing a deeper collapse. News of replacement gives that discrepancy new stakes.
beats.trace: Crew stress + allocation → relief action → lower stress and lost productive time → observed discipline changes → distinct supervisor interpretations. Cathexis influence requires a real contact or action.

beats.name: The report becomes a survival strategy
beats.caption: Original Security confrontation as a relationship reference. Replacement decisions are not depicted facts.
beats.condition: The replacement rumour reaches supervisors through recorded channels near the end of Act 1. They interpret the proposed criteria through their own record.
beats.minds: Stiletto can point to repair downtime; Limen to ignored warnings; Thrum to recovered workers. No account alone describes the whole run.
beats.action: Each may defend a colleague, disclose a previously withheld fact, refuse the preferred story or shift blame. Select from their actual beliefs and commitments.
beats.change: The player’s earlier reassurances and accusations now constrain whom they can credibly retain or remove.
beats.next: The episode culminates in a changed allocation of authority or a binding new promise. Its unresolved costs enter Act 2; a fair decision need not satisfy everyone.
beats.trace: Rumour receipt → perceived personal threat → selected protective or accusatory plan → delivered statement → player response. Log protection as carefully as betrayal.

views: Follow an action backward to evidence, interpretation and commitment, then forward to physical and social consequences. Distinguish observed causes from a character’s attribution.
Show each supervisor’s changing intention, stress, self-confidence and important memories across the same beats. Mark the specific event that changed each state.
Show who learned which version, from whom and when; where a report was rejected, suppressed or never delivered. Repeated hearsay retains its common origin.
Compose the episode from supported actions and suitable assets. Every recap beat links to its evidence; distinguish a narrator’s account from a character’s subjective account.
episodes.access: The author or developer can inspect the full trace. Act 1 players see only their available evidence and reports. Brain 2.0 may expose deeper mental state according to the agreed reveal; it does not grant the player an omniscient debug console by accident.
assembly: Track unresolved commitments, hazards, grievances and knowledge gaps as continuing threads. Group events by these links, not merely by occurring on the same day.
Recognize a turning point when a decision changes an intention, relationship or operating arrangement. Show the earlier promise or pressure that makes the change meaningful.
Allow competence, restraint, cooperation and recovery to form satisfying episodes. Avoiding a disaster must not produce an empty report or provoke a forced new crisis.
Let the episode layer choose emphasis, pacing and viewpoints after events are recorded. It cannot add a betrayal, reroll damage or change motives to improve the ending.
Treat a revelation as new access to an existing fact or recorded private act. It may change a character’s judgment of history; it must not rewrite that history.
If a run is dull, revise the underlying pressures, available commitments or presentation during design. Do not secretly punish a successful player to manufacture drama.
episodes.quality: A strong episode lets the viewer recognize each supervisor, follow what each stood to lose, identify a consequential decision and trace the aftermath. A polished recap without those connections fails the Producer Vision.
episodes.sourceBoundary: The Producer Vision supplies the dramatic north star and demand for observability. Stagemaker supplies the separation between simulation and visual episode composition. The old Emotional Arc Engine was read-only; the new behavioural BDI proposal intentionally goes further. Narrative records what a character believed or claimed without promoting that account to physical truth.
checks: Select an action: can we show its actual decision inputs without inventing a motive?
Select a claim: can we trace its audience and source, including failed transmission?
Select a later refusal: can we point to the earlier order, injury, promise or interpretation that matters?
Select a recap beat or image: which recorded event or clearly marked viewpoint supports it?
Review a safe, competent run: does it show meaningful character choices and a coherent arc without forced sabotage?
Change only presentation: do the underlying event history and outcome remain identical?

experience.title: Watch, understand, intervene
experience.intro: A whole routine day targets about one minute, two to three for heavier days. The next prototype centres operation in a common cinematic 3D factory: each room supplies a distinct puzzle, while adviser choice, structured briefings, incidents and allocation use focused interfaces. The Conveyor mini-game tab specifies the first proposal; the current runtime remains the earlier illustrated-console baseline. The procedural commissioning study now uses Babylon.js in a separate route. One persistent factory camera serves night construction and production playback. The eighteen-hour shift / six-hour charge baseline and three-second illustrated day/phase interludes are approved direction. The existing first-shift game protocol is unchanged.
experience.rhythmStatus: Agreed: paused planning, continuous shifts and consequential decision pauses. Whole-day target: about one minute routine, two to three at most for heavier days.
rhythm: At night, use the last result to keep or change the physical arrangement. Preview and commit eligible construction before the morning briefing. A sound floor needs no compulsory purchase or edit. First entry is the guided Lobby–Security–Lattice setup.

After night construction, read the compact factory facts. On the first morning, answer leadership and acknowledge the weekly quota, then choose LIMEN or STILETTO. Their assessment and proposed assignments use the actual commissioned layout. Later mornings reuse yesterday’s result without repeating the full report. Reading and transitions count toward the daily budget.

The simulation advances during the shift. In the current prototype, room artwork, readouts, attributed reports, effects and sound communicate committed production, wear and actions. Later, the 3D viewer also shows their continuous spatial execution.

Events in the chosen adviser’s assigned room resolve automatically under their authority. A response decision elsewhere or at factory level pauses at a defined boundary with their recommendation selected; the player accepts or overrides, then watches the consequences.

Preview and permanently commit the factory/quota split. Show one useful benefit, known cost and live issue, then reuse that result as tomorrow’s context instead of repeating the full report. Payment timing remains open.
views: Six room positions, compact facts, calls and supervisor communication. The next opening reaches this console on the morning after night setup. Leadership must be acknowledged before adviser selection. Locked room screens remain dark; the cinematic floor owns construction and operation.

One shared 3D world shows room puzzles, worker tasks, machinery, queues and interventions over authoritative ticks. Room focus and build/inspection overlays support operation; switching views does not pause the world. Repair still requires engineering.

A timeline connects visible incidents to earlier warnings, reports and commitments. Illustrated accounts support the first prototype; spatial replays can join later. Player evidence stays knowledge-filtered, while development tools can inspect complete traces.
experience.shared: Room scenes, decision interfaces and the later 3D view share room/event identity, committed state and the command path. Switching views preserves context. Closing or disabling a visual layer cannot create a second simulation, lose a pending decision or remove the means to finish the shift.
example: Later Act 1 example, with Witch available: a known conveyor hazard becomes a jam. The illustrated room shows a matching stopped-line scene and a persistent incident entry. The future 3D view can depict the same halt. Neither view may reveal an unseen event through an omniscient cut.
The inspector separates observed damage, prior warnings and a supervisor’s account. Act 1 does not expose hidden loyalty, internal stress scores or true motives.

If the event belongs to the chosen adviser’s assigned room, their response resolves automatically and is recorded. Otherwise pause for a player response with the adviser’s recommendation selected. A restart, repair or override is validated and recorded; disclosure choices determine who learns what.

Resume the shift. Committed work, lost output and attributed reactions update the room scene, instruments and record. A later consultation can respond to that experience. The future 3D layer animates the same recorded execution; it is not required to understand the consequence.
clocks: Fixed logical steps own cause and effect. Do not resolve an entire shift in advance if the player can change its course midway. Tick frequency is a later systems decision.
Interpolate between delivered states; stretch a transition or replay an incident without inventing new outcomes. A held last frame is not continuous simulation.
Rendering speed, network delay and model latency do not define factory rules. The host paces ticks and records admitted external inputs. Slower hardware must not produce different accidents.

About one minute for the whole routine day, two to three for a heavier day. Count required reading, decisions and transitions; this does not change deterministic logical time or impose response deadlines.
experience.pauseBoundary: Pause for a consequential choice outside delegated authority; automatic acts leave receipts without asking for confirmation. Group routine reports and preserve pending decisions during inspection. The current viewer runs only on the factory/room views; reading surfaces suspend advance requests. Such UI pauses do not consume production opportunity. Event granularity and future handover rules remain open.
experience.mobile: Keep the complete adviser → plan → incident → allocation loop usable on a phone through focused, asset-driven panels. Preserve the quota, current speaker, affected room and pause state; avoid shrinking a desktop console into unreadable controls. Artwork can crop or use dedicated variants while text and touch targets reflow. The future 3D view needs its own device budget and can be unavailable without blocking play.
migration: The original Director Console spec and implementation provide six illustrated camera feeds, gunmetal and glass textures, a status plate, resource icon variants, a command deck and focused incident surfaces. Audit and adapt those actual assets and modules before inventing replacements.
Sim4: reference for the later live view

The existing Sim4 plugin reconstructs snapshots/diffs; its Pixi scene uses world positions, room bounds, floor selection and interpolated movement. That is an implemented isometric viewer, not an existing finished 3D renderer. Sim5 documents describe broader viewer plans.

Reuse the old Lobby–Dispatch–Security and Dispatch–Neural Lattice spatial connections, visual language and protocol patterns. Do not inherit its day-based unlocks, economy or exposed psychology. Night construction precedes morning advice; no first-day assignments exist before authorization.

Room-card loading and the supervisor interaction archive are sources, not a complete state-to-scene map. Identify room, participants, action, visible outcome and permitted knowledge for each selection. Never show unrelated disaster art merely because it looks dramatic.
art: Use authored artwork for almost every visible game element: rooms, supervisors, bezels, plates, controls, resource symbols, meters, dossiers, incident framing and allocation machinery. Begin with sim-sim assets. Native text, semantics and hit areas remain for legibility, keyboard access and responsive layout.

Prepare coherent normal, hover/focus, pressed, selected, disabled and alarm treatments where meaningful. Preserve perspective, light direction and material scale. Reuse textures and sliced frames rather than stretching a whole painted panel; a generic card with a texture pasted behind it is not the target.

Use code for layout, masking, transitions, restrained lighting, glass/noise, indicators and event feedback. These support authored surfaces. A future genuine live 3D scene may render geometry, materials and spatial light procedurally; that exception does not justify replacing the present interface art with generic CSS shapes.

Inventory missing assets by interface role and state. Reuse suitable art, then generate what adviser choice, briefings, incidents and allocation actually require. A clearly marked neutral placeholder with accurate event text is acceptable during development; unrelated art and polished-looking fake outcomes are not.

When building the live view, use real floors, walls, machines and occluders where spatial lighting needs them. Painted images cannot supply arbitrary camera angles or correct moving shadows by themselves. This is future scene work, not a prerequisite for the current playable interfaces.

renderer.title: Future live 3D view: a renderer candidate, not a prototype dependency
renderer.status: Future research · comparison dated 7 October 2026 · selection unconfirmed
renderer.why: The present prototype uses asset-driven interfaces and illustrated cameras in the existing React application. For the later cinematic factory, Babylon.js remains the first proposed 3D candidate under a controlled camera; Three.js / React Three Fiber is an alternative. Recheck the dated capability research and benchmark representative art before choosing. No 3D framework is selected or required for this interface pass.
rows: Integrated 3D scene and authoring tools, including the current lighting and Inspector improvements. The attraction is a coherent visual toolset; scene performance still needs measurement.

A flexible 3D scene composed within React. Three supports WebGPU with a WebGL 2 backend fallback; Fiber supports supplying that renderer. Attractive for bespoke scene composition, with effects and addon compatibility to verify.
Best reuse for a layered 2D route

Already used by the old viewer. Strong fit for sprites and existing painted art; spatial light and shadow would require additional techniques. Its stable guide recommends WebGL for production and describes WebGPU as experimental.
Supports standalone engine use as well as its editor, with WebGPU/WebGL 2 paths. Worth reconsidering if visual scene authoring becomes the dominant workflow; not ruled out by capability.

A capable 2D game framework with a new WebGL renderer and lighting system. Our external simulation and spatial lighting favour a rendering-focused 3D choice; Phaser 4’s migration guide lists removal of its former 3D helpers.
renderer.boundary: The dated renderer comparison is research, not an installed stack or a benchmark. The next prototype requires a common cinematic factory, while the final renderer selection still needs a representative room spike and device tests. The old viewer supplies protocol and observation patterns, not a finished 3D scene.
renderer.performance: Budget the expensive effects around the focal event: a few shadow-casting lights, reusable worker instances, restrained transparent smoke, cached static detail and bounded render resolution. Offer measured quality tiers with the same visual identity. Verify WebGL 2 and WebGPU paths on target devices; neither the API label nor a feature list establishes speed.
spike: Build one representative conveyor bay with existing art, proxy geometry, workers, a moving batch and the alarm light. Test source–obstacle–surface alignment and moving reflections before adding more effects.

After the interface prototype is useful on its own, drive the 3D bay from a recorded state/event fixture. Show the same event and identifiers in the illustrated overview and live scene, open the same decision interface, and replay without changing the outcome.
Inspect desktop and mobile frame times, memory, initial loading, input response and graphics recovery. Check the busiest credible incident, not an empty demo.
Compare a Three.js alternative only if this scene exposes a material limitation. Approve the visual result and device budget before expanding the factory.

scope: Asset-driven leadership, adviser, briefing, assignment, incident and allocation interfaces exist with illustrated rooms. Preserve their functional contracts without treating that baseline as the full spatial game.
Next prototype: one spatial room puzzle

An editable conveyor chain, individual workers and machinery, real-time fixed ticks, physical upgrades, local policy and supervisor delegation. The common cinematic view becomes the operating surface. Prove one room before committing to five simultaneous puzzles.

Focused interfaces and spatial views consume the same knowledge-filtered events and submit validated commands. A headless kernel remains possible; no animation, sound or model response creates world facts. The rendered operating prototype must prove spatial feedback, not rely on an unrelated decorative scene.

engineBoundary.title: One simulation, replaceable viewers and models
engineBoundary.intro: The engine owns the factory. KVP exposes an explicit view of it. Model services interpret permitted context and offer bounded contributions. A concrete end-to-end prototype must prove these separations. The visual fixture has its own pure typed command/tick kernel and a replaceable local host; it is public test state, not the private first-shift run.
engineBoundary.status: Agreed direction · frontend independence and Rust-native logic
planes: World state, production, BDI state, information propagation, command validation and authoritative ticks.
Versioned KVP messages: permitted snapshots, ordered diffs, events, decisions and command results.

Current asset-driven adviser, order, incident, allocation and record interfaces with illustrated rooms; later a live 3D factory and spatial replay. Every client reconstructs permitted state and submits commands through the same boundary.
Context requests leave through a separate service contract. Recorded, validated proposals may enter only at specified decision boundaries.
rust: Stable entity IDs, typed components and tagged commands/events. Model absence and failure explicitly. Store references by ID rather than passing mutable object graphs between systems.
Systems receive bounded read views and emit command buffers. An ordered commit phase owns writes. Declare read/write sets before considering parallel execution.
Fix system order, tie-breaking and random streams. Keep wall clocks, network calls and renderer state outside the kernel. Record external inputs before they affect a step.
Define integer bounds, overflow, rounding, fixed-point or quantized values, canonical ordering and serialization. JavaScript numbers and Python integers do not automatically match Rust semantics.
Validation produces typed acceptance or rejection with a reason. Missing context, stale commands and failed model requests take named paths rather than silently mutating state.

Run headless fixtures and invariant checks from the start. A future Rust implementation must match the same command outcomes, events and canonical state hashes. Types alone do not guarantee equivalence.
kvp: KVP-0001 defines a transport-independent kernel–viewer boundary with primitive payloads, version negotiation, ordered state reconstruction and replay. Neither side imports the other’s runtime.

Publish a player projection that excludes hidden Act 1 state. Developer traces use a separate privileged projection. Filter before transport; hiding fields in the UI is insufficient. Hash and resync each projection consistently.

Identify the run, command and intended state/decision boundary. Validate ordering, duplication and stale inputs; report acceptance or rejection. The client cannot make an assignment true by animating it.
Scene nodes, meshes, camera coordinates and shader parameters belong to the viewer. Protocol data can identify spatial facts and semantic actions without importing Babylon, Pixi or React types.

The old live client uses SIM_INPUT and records input acknowledgements as events; older guidelines describe INPUT_COMMAND and separate acknowledgements. Reconcile code and tests before migration, and version semantic changes. Do not silently claim the old schema covers the new game.
llm: Request a role such as interpretation, consultation or recap through our own schema. Adapters translate to OpenAI initially and other hosted or open models later. SDK objects and provider errors stop at the adapter.

Build context from that character’s observations, memories and beliefs. Private truth is not available merely because the service can query the database. Player-facing dialogue uses the permitted disclosure policy.

A model may suggest a belief update or bounded intention. The admission layer checks schema, evidence references, permissible changes, staleness and timing. Only the kernel applies an accepted contribution. Fluent prose cannot award production, invent casualties or rewrite history.

Keep retrieval, prompt management, model routing, batching and evaluation outside the kernel. Use the JavaScript or Python ecosystem where it helps; changing that service must not require a sim or frontend rewrite.

Schedule meaningful decision requests rather than per-tick calls. Budget by run and request type, cap context/output, cache only under matching context and version keys, and provide deterministic fallback policies. Routine factory ticks do not wait for narration.

Check contract validity, knowledge leakage, character consistency, supported claims, useful variation, cost and latency. If outputs can influence state, also compare admitted decisions and downstream run outcomes across a fixed scenario suite. An API-compatible replacement is not automatically behaviourally equivalent.
engineBoundary.determinism: A replay is defined by initial state, rules version, random seed and ordered accepted external inputs—including model contributions and admission/fallback decisions. Replaying those records is deterministic. Calling a live model again is not promised to reproduce them. A stricter seed-and-player-inputs-only mode must freeze or exclude outcome-affecting model contributions.
engineBoundary.timing: Late responses cannot alter committed history. Requests carry their context revision and admissible boundary; the host records acceptance, rejection or fallback. Slow verbal delivery can arrive later as presentation only when it cannot change the choice or its meaning. Player-facing cadence is a separate budget: the entire day targets about a minute, two to three for heavier days. Tick rate, simulation outcomes and model admission remain independent of that presentation target. UI reading pauses are not in-world lost production.
engineBoundary.prototype: The implemented first-day build uses a pure TypeScript kernel, explicit HTTP snapshots/diffs and a React viewer. The next conveyor proposal adds spatial machine/task state, fixed-tick operation, construction and shared policies behind a versioned contract. The common 3D operating view and existing focused decision interfaces consume that state; no renderer dependency enters the kernel. Model integration remains independent and must demonstrate value over the deterministic baseline.
proof: Now: replay a fixture headlessly and through the illustrated decision interfaces; authoritative results match and the complete loop works without a graphics scene. Later: run the same fixture through the 3D view and compare the same event/command results.
Disable or delay the model service; the factory continues with recorded fallback behaviour.
Run without a graphics context; production, knowledge and supervisor actions still resolve.
Recover a viewer from a fresh snapshot and ordered diffs without changing the run.
Verify that an Act 1 client never receives hidden worker statistics or privileged causal traces.
Measure visual performance independently from simulation correctness and model quality.

Expression labels remain authoring/test coverage, not inferred player traits. A scenario’s physical outcome and received memories must produce its visible payoff; the UI or model cannot invent recognition to compensate for absent mechanics.
engineBoundary.sourceBoundary: The old Sim4 specification already describes a Rust-aligned kernel, narrative sidecar and integration phase. Current code shows phased scheduling and command buffers, but some integration phases are described as stubs. Preserve the boundary doctrine; do not assume the complete new BDI or live-model pipeline already exists. The working old world viewer is Sim4/KVP feeding a Pixi isometric scene; Sim5’s Web/Godot/Unreal documents are strategy drafts. Preserve their replaceable-viewer doctrine without claiming a finished inherited 3D implementation.

loops.title: From a second to a session
loops.intro: Build at night, choose whose judgment to trust in the morning, operate the prepared factory, then decide what output to keep. Evidence from that day informs the next night. The routine whole cycle targets about one minute; heavier days take two to three.
loops.status: Agreed cadence · proposed interface budget · runtime unchanged
loops.boundary: One second describes immediate feedback. One minute is the routine night-and-day cycle, including ordinary construction decisions, advice, approval, operation and allocation. The guided arrival is a one-time onboarding arc, measured explicitly in first-day elapsed time. Heavier days target two to three minutes; reading has no deadline. Thirty minutes spans multiple days and delivery cycles.
cycle: At night, use the last result to keep or change the physical arrangement. Preview and commit eligible construction before the morning briefing. A sound floor needs no compulsory purchase or edit.
Read the useful change, installed capacity and remaining weekly obligation. The first morning introduces the weekly mandate after the guided build; later mornings use the previous result.
Compare current short pitches, inspect the known tradeoff and appoint one adviser. This is the daily choice of whose judgment to trust, after preparing the physical factory.
Read the structured assessment and proposed arrangement for the prepared floor. Accept or override assignments with delegated authority visible. Detailed placement controls remain optional.

Watch the common cinematic factory, adjust flow and see physical consequences. The adviser acts automatically in their assigned room; consequential decisions elsewhere pause for acceptance or override.
Permanently split completed robots between factory and weekly quota. Known losses, queues, wear and people carry into the next night’s building decisions.

scales.name: Read the living factory
scales.question: Is this working as I intended?
scales.player: Follow a batch or supervisor, notice a change, or select something to inspect. Most seconds require no input. Consequential decisions pause, so a missed visual cue is not a reflex penalty.
scales.system: Batches, worker tasks, access routes, machine queues, equipment condition and supervisor actions drive continuous feedback. The next spatial conveyor proposal needs explicit station processing and worker task state, while keeping staffing automated rather than adding station allocation sliders.
scales.feedback: In the current prototype, artwork state, readable instruments, physical control response, sound and persistent incident cues show accepted, queued, rejected and completed actions. Resolved adviser-room events remain visible; decisions elsewhere bring forward a response interface. The future 3D view adds continuous belt, queue and posture changes over the same events.
scales.reward: The pleasure of a dense machine working, and recognition of a person’s characteristic behaviour. Visual variation helps identify meaningful changes.
scales.carry: A visible hesitation or growing queue becomes a question for the minute loop. Inspection retains the event and its source rather than demanding the player remember a fleeting animation.
scales.example: Limen’s procedure or Stiletto’s output policy changes the confirmed production and condition readouts. A matching illustrated room state and recorded report ground the result. Future spatial motion can show the different cadence; present feedback must work without it.
scales.failure: A constant spectacle with no readable state is noise. A click required every second turns direction into busywork. Neither should be the main source of difficulty.

scales.name: Direct one factory day
scales.question: Whose judgment will I back today, and what did it cost?
scales.player: Read the useful starting context, choose today’s adviser, hear their concise assessment and approve or revise the arrangement. Run the shift, accept or override event recommendations outside their delegated room, then permanently allocate output and carry the result into tomorrow. This whole sequence targets about one minute; heavier days take two to three at most.
scales.system: The chosen adviser sets the priority and automatic authority in their assigned room. Production, equipment condition, individual workers and supervisor memories evolve through deterministic work and admitted choices. The day settles output to factory or weekly quota without resetting its consequences.
scales.feedback: Use short pitches, structured advice and concrete actions before commitment. During operation, distinguish automatic acts from decisions awaiting the player. End with completed output, known cost and a relevant reaction or outstanding issue; tomorrow reuses this result without repeating the full report.
scales.reward: A complete daily decision pays off: the factory made progress, a tradeoff became visible and the next adviser choice has context.
scales.carry: Retained workers, committed quota, wear, memories and unresolved issues persist. Early relief does not repair damage. Later engineering, conditioning and information dynamics deepen the same daily cadence.
scales.example: Choose Stiletto for output, approve her arrangement, observe her automatic Conveyor response, decide whether to back or override her Security recommendation, then split today’s completed robots between factory and quota. The resulting wear and reactions give tomorrow’s choice meaning.
scales.failure: A minute of production followed by several minutes of mandatory menus misses the pace. Reading every supervisor’s full brief, repeating yesterday’s report or confirming every automatic act creates busywork. Quiet successful days remain valid, with no compulsory accident or repair action.

scales.name: Establish a way of running the place
scales.question: What kind of factory did my successful decisions create?
scales.player: Across several days, choose advisers whose judgment seems suited to the known situation. Learn what their priorities achieve, accept or override their actions, and carry the resulting production and relationships into later choices.
scales.system: Workers and supervisors retain history. Daily permanent allocations build capacity or weekly quota progress; equipment condition and relationship consequences carry forward. Engineering joins those tradeoffs in Part 03.
scales.feedback: Connect the session’s end to its beginning: committed quota progress, retained workers, changed equipment condition and a supervisor whose method you backed. Later sessions may also show engineering work; the recap uses actual history.
scales.reward: Competence plus authorship: “I can run this place, and this is how I chose to run it.” An earned new capability can open the next problem; a recovered setback can provide an equally complete session arc.
scales.carry: Save the exact factory, people, commitments and unresolved matters. A session boundary does not reset relationships, reroll incidents or manufacture an ending.
scales.example: Across early delivery cycles, Limen’s procedures preserve the line but limit output. Retaining completed robots strengthens the factory while leaving more quota for later. Choosing Stiletto on a later day changes the operating approach, while prior commitments and wear remain.
scales.failure: Thirty minutes of unrelated alerts has no arc. Thirty minutes without a visible payoff feels like preparation for a game that has not started. A session need not complete Act 1 or Brain 2.0.

shift.intro: One shift is the whole daily loop: about one minute for routine play, two to three for heavier days. Preparation, running, decisions and settlement all share that budget.
beats: Night construction
At night, use the last result to keep or change the physical arrangement. Preview and commit eligible construction before the morning briefing. A sound floor needs no compulsory purchase or edit.
Paused plan

After night construction, read the compact factory facts. On the first morning, answer leadership and acknowledge the weekly quota, then choose LIMEN or STILETTO. Their assessment and proposed assignments use the actual commissioned layout. Later mornings reuse yesterday’s result without repeating the full report. Accept or override placements before releasing the shift.
Continuous operation

The chosen adviser recommends responses throughout continuous operation and automatically resolves events in their assigned room. Routine notices record those actions. Other supervisors retain their roles, interpretations and ability to respond.
Consequential interruption

For response decisions outside the adviser’s room, pause with their proposed resolution selected. Accept or override it. Every supervisor interprets the decision when they witness or learn of it; the response can affect respect, loyalty and confidence.
Settle and carry forward

Account for completed output and known losses. Permanently split today’s production between factory and quota; show remaining weekly obligation and days left. Review development commitments when relevant. Payment timing is separate and unresolved.
shift.target: Owner direction: a routine game day lasts about one minute; a heavier day takes two to three minutes at most, including ordinary reading, decisions and transitions. The older three-shifts-per-thirty-minutes proposal is discarded. Leadership calls and introductions must fit the longer-day allowance. Optional inspection remains available without becoming required work. Progression still requires mastery; validate this cadence against the roughly 10–20 minute full-floor unlock target.
shift.density: Each day has one primary adviser choice, a concise plan and enough visible work to feel its result. Add consequential interruptions only when warranted. The UI budget includes every required screen, caption and transition; do not spend it on repeated summaries or automatic-action confirmations.
dayBudget: Keep the working arrangement or commit one prepared change. Longer construction choices use the heavier-day allowance.
Current pitches, appointment and structured assessment of the prepared floor. Weekly calls add time.
Accept the plan or open detailed overrides. No inherited day-one assignments.
Watch actual work, intervene where useful and pause for warranted decisions.
Commit the permanent output split; reuse known consequences as next night’s context.

controls: Choose the adviser, who selects the daily priority and proposes assignments. Accept or override particular placements. Overrides are remembered challenges to their judgment; the proposal remains distinct from the actual orders and their execution.

Proposed next loop: place purchased machinery, alter connections and worker access, set a room policy, and operate pace/feed controls. Construction costs money and simulated downtime. General policies apply per room; repair remains unavailable until engineering.

The adviser resolves events in their assigned room automatically. Elsewhere, accept or override available responses. Repair enters that set only with engineering in Part 03; stopping or slowing before then cannot restore condition.
Back a supervisor, challenge an explanation or set a boundary. Mechanical orders resolve when accepted and feasible; appeals for cooperation may be refused through a logged decision.

The daily adviser supplies interpretation and recommendations. Question, reassure or challenge them without replacing their priority. The same adviser covers daytime events; relevant disclosure choices affect who learns and reacts.

Commit completed robots to the factory or weekly quota. Every confirmed split is permanent; retained workers cannot later rescue a delivery shortage. Money and development use their own defined transactions.
layers: 1 · Material flow
Where is the line constrained?
Room production, completed output, worker counts and equipment condition. The conveyor’s visible stations do not imply separate staffing controls.
Present from the start. First make the physical cause readable.
2 · Delegated authority
Whose method am I relying on?
Limen and Stiletto pursue different priorities; the same order can provoke different actions.
Also present from the start. Introduce personalities through work before explaining a psychology model.
3 · Strain and recovery
What is the operation consuming?
Work pressure, wear and stress affect capability and responses. Relief or prevention costs productive capacity.
Early operation reveals strain and physical cost. Engineering repair appears in Part 03 and Thrum’s specialist relief later; hidden worker history already exists.
4 · Accounts and beliefs
Who knows, believes or reports what?
Witnesses, reports and rumours influence interpretation. Claims may fail to spread or be believed.
Surface when a relevant disagreement, incident or contact occurs. Do not require an accident to teach incomplete information.
5 · Memory and commitment
Why did yesterday’s solution change today’s response?
Honoured promises, blame, respect and confidence influence later intentions.
Close the feedback loop across shifts. Introduce deeper inspection only when the game permits it.
6 · Investment and capability
What can this factory attempt next?
Retention and income finance capacity or another room, adding a new tension.
Unlock through mastery. Add one new decision family at a time rather than another independent maintenance meter.
loops.coupling: These are views of connected state, not six standalone minigames. Pressure changes work; work produces evidence; people interpret that evidence; their next actions alter work. Money and workforce counts keep the consequences concrete.
feedbacks: Completed output → permanent factory allocation → usable workforce capacity → future output. Committing output to the weekly quota gives up that internal contribution. More workers help only where the factory can use them.
Pressure → wear and stress → poorer operation or hazardous decisions → output shortfall → temptation to push harder. Its escape routes must remain visible before terminal failure.
Back a method → supervisor confidence and a witnessed precedent → more initiative of that kind → a result the player must own, correct or defend.
Incident or claim → selective exposure and interpretation → changed trust or stress → different behaviour → new evidence and further accounts.

opening.title: The unassigned opening and the first weekly quota
opening.note: Agreed opening rules; example trajectories and mastery checks remain proposals. A session need not cover the whole week, and reaching the week’s end does not automatically unlock the Theatre.
beats: Read the starting facts

Enter the producer console with funds, workers, condition, empty assignments and two available rooms. Answer leadership and acknowledge the weekly quota before selecting an adviser. Keep this opening within the longer-day allowance.
Choose the first adviser

Introduce Limen’s safety and compliance approach and Stiletto’s productivity approach, with understandable costs. The chosen adviser selects the priority and proposes the initial arrangement; the player may override assignments.
Run the arrangement

Start the continuous shift. Their assigned room has automatic event authority; elsewhere their recommendations can be overridden. Observe output and actual consequences. Repair is not an early control.
Commit the day’s output
Allocate completed robots to the factory or weekly quota, with clear before/after totals and an irreversible commitment. A proposed default may help, but the allocation remains the player’s decision.
Carry the result into tomorrow

Review hard facts and choose the next adviser. Safety, output and adaptive balance have different consequences as the deadline approaches. Cathexis arrives when the capability gate is earned, not because a session or week ended.

branches.name: Protect the line
branches.choice: Choose Limen and support preventive procedures; commit scarce daily output between growth and quota.
branches.gain: Avoid or reduce the hazard and preserve the workforce. The factory becomes more predictable.
branches.cost: Lower output and earning potential leave fewer robots for both destinations. Stiletto has a concrete throughput objection.
branches.echo: Preserved equipment remains useful through Part 02 and may need less engineering time when Witch arrives. The early workforce still lacks Theatre indoctrination.
branches.test: The safety path must remain capable of progress. An injury is not required to create tension, expense or a consequential disagreement.

branches.name: Protect the delivery
branches.choice: Choose Stiletto and back her productive approach; decide how much of the larger output to retain permanently.
branches.gain: More near-term output can meet an obligation or finance the next improvement. The gamble can succeed.
branches.cost: Wear and exposure persist through Parts 01–02. More retained workers cannot repair the line; an accident can reduce the capacity needed to finish the week.
branches.echo: Witch may later inherit substantial damage while Cathexis inherits the workers’ experiences. Neither outcome is erased by changing advisers.
branches.test: An accident is not a scripted punishment for this choice. Repeated exposure should raise comprehensible risk; success must not erase the underlying cost.

branches.name: Adapt as the week develops
branches.choice: Start with either adviser, then choose later advisers and overrides in response to actual results.
branches.gain: Preserve capacity when needed and use it for output when justified.
branches.cost: The earlier allocation and physical costs remain; advisers and other supervisors remember overrides.
branches.echo: The next specialists encounter the pattern of decisions, not a neutral reset between Limen and Stiletto.
branches.test: Balance is viable but not a universally optimal alternating sequence. It adds no third adviser or priority selector.

laterSessions: Cathexis encounters an existing workforce, including early unindoctrinated cohorts. Conditioning interacts with the operating approach already established; better coordination can strengthen her independent audience.

Witch introduces engineering and the Brewery together. Repairing inherited damage competes for her time with turning conveyor waste into substrate; earlier supervisor combinations shape the response to downtime.
Precision, scarce expertise and genuine stress relief compete for time. Smart-worker sales versus retention make an immediate gain oppose future capacity.
Existing work and memories acquire new stakes when replacement rumours spread. Apparent performance and actual contribution diverge. The full-run resolution is outside this session pass.
loops.llm: Production ticks and routine event resolution need no model call. Morning briefings are the first candidate for useful interpretation across observations and memories. Compare authored BDI, that baseline with generated prose, and admitted model reasoning. Use reasoning only if it improves meaningful advice and consequences; validate and record contributions, bound cost and latency, and retain a complete playable fallback.
guardrails: Communicate the purpose, known cost and observable result of the player’s choices. Hidden simulation depth should create enjoyable decisions without requiring mastery of all its calculations. The owner’s first prototype playtest is the initial acceptance gate.
Budget the whole day, not only conveyor runtime. About 60 seconds routine, two to three minutes for heavier days; protect adviser choice by removing redundant navigation and repeated exposition.
A stable factory can be satisfying to watch. Add pressure through meaningful constraints, not guaranteed failures or an obligation to click.
Changes have costs in work, time and remembered treatment. Do not add an action-point currency merely to stop assignment spam.
A short debrief identifies one causal lesson and one live issue. Preserve deeper traces for inspection without making routine play a log-reading job.
Safe and aggressive operating methods both need viable choices and characteristic liabilities. Neither is universally correct.
Keep the first slice to conveyor, Security, Limen, Stiletto, simple money/workforce accounting and one consequential recovery path. Defer new rooms and rich dialogue until this loop is playable.
tests: Can a routine day be completed around one minute with all required reading and transitions included?
Do consequential days, weekly calls and introductions fit two to three minutes without rushing comprehension?
Can the player explain whom they trusted, what changed, what it cost and what they will consider tomorrow?
After a short glance, can the player identify whether the line is flowing and where the immediate problem is?
After a local intervention, can they explain what changed, what it cost and why holding the plan was or was not viable?
Across shifts, can they recognize a supervisor’s response to an earlier decision without seeing hidden loyalty numbers?
At session end, can they name a concrete accomplishment, a cost they accepted and a question worth returning to?
Does a safe run produce a coherent session without a compulsory accident?
Do runs with recorded model outputs or deterministic fallbacks remain understandable and mechanically complete?
Can players explain before the shift that choosing the adviser selects today’s priority and automatic authority in their assigned room?
Can they distinguish yesterday’s direct facts from the adviser’s additional claims, and later recognize how an override affected different supervisors?
Does the opening foreground adviser choice before any assignments, without exposing repair or station-staffing controls?
Does daily allocation clearly show irreversible factory/weekly-quota commitments without implying payment at an unagreed time?
Can the asset-driven interfaces and illustrated scenes carry the entire loop, its atmosphere and understandable consequences with no live 3D viewer?

uiDesign.title: UI and simulation complexity
uiDesign.intro: The next prototype combines a common cinematic operating view with focused asset-driven decision interfaces. Engine depth, player knowledge, interface load and visual fidelity are separate axes. Spatial machinery and worker tasks can be mechanically rich while the player sees one useful operating question. The whole routine day targets about one minute, two to three for heavier days; optional depth must not create a longer mandatory reading route.
axes: How much causally relevant state exists: individual workers, wear, stress, beliefs, intentions, relationships and memory.
Which facts, reports and interpretations the director can access. This depends on observation, disclosure and progression.
Which interventions are available, whose cooperation they need and when they can take effect. Knowledge does not automatically grant control.
How much the player must read, compare or operate at once. Group, prioritize and progressively reveal detail without erasing the underlying state.

Authored art, physical materials, responsive controls, sound and later spatial animation. High visual quality does not require more player chores, more revealed statistics or a more complicated simulation.
uiDesign.principle: True system complexity, revealed information and the effort required to play are different things. Brain 2.0 can reveal more of an existing society without making every hidden variable a gauge. Keep communication as simple as the decision allows, and judge the result by the playing experience.
knowledge: An available sensor or witnessed event establishes a fact, such as the line having stopped. Make the evidence inspectable.
A named supervisor or worker makes a claim. Preserve who said it, when and what they could know. The UI does not certify it as truth.
A forecast or explanation drawn from available evidence. State uncertainty and distinguish it from both an observation and a quotation.
Do not send or render undiscovered states, motives or the replacement purpose. Absence of evidence is not a zero value or proof that nothing happened.

Missing indoctrination exists from production, but is not directly exposed in Act 1. An informed supervisor may report or infer it. Act 2 direct inspection uses the preserved history, including actual later Theatre participation.
surfaces: Current day and phase, weekly quota progress and deadline, money, workforce counts and foreground issue. Do not reveal repair controls or worker conditioning state before their intended unlocks.

The common operating view shows actual worker tasks, machinery and room puzzles. The six-room console handles summary and communication. Both select the same known entities and events and lead to focused decision interfaces. This is the next prototype direction; the current runtime uses illustrated rooms.
The selected problem, its known evidence, available actions and relevant history. It expands on demand rather than placing every trait in the main view.
A paused consequential choice: what requires a decision, whose account is shown, known costs and uncertainty. Keep the scene’s context visible.

A primary daily adviser selection followed by assessment, context, their priority and proposed arrangement. Responses and placement overrides affect relationships. The adviser continues proposing event responses during the shift.
A compact accomplishment, cost and unresolved thread, with optional causal inspection. A developer view can go deeper than the player’s knowledge permits.

mechanics.name: Conveyor and Security
mechanics.see: Individual workers, machinery, intake/assembly/outtake queues, routes and crossings; Security changes who reaches a post and when.
mechanics.do: Build or improve the chain at night. In the morning choose an adviser and accept or override assignments and local policy; during operation use pace/feed controls. Adviser-room incident authority remains automatic; responses elsewhere can be overridden.
mechanics.engine: Explicit task, route, machine, batch and worker component state is required for the proposed spatial puzzle. Detailed processing is simulated; staffing remains automated. The current first-day kernel does not implement this room puzzle.
mechanics.carry: Completed output, wear, delayed work and witnessed overrides change the next local problem.
mechanics.uiCost: One focused floor, contextual machinery inspector and paused construction view. One operating question at a time; no per-worker or station staffing grid.

mechanics.name: Quota, cash and worker retention
mechanics.see: Today’s completed robots, workforce count, committed quota progress, remaining weekly obligation and deadline. Funds and actual development commitments are separate.
mechanics.do: Preview and confirm the daily split between factory and weekly quota. Spend money on eligible development. Engineering assignment becomes possible with Witch; it is not an early repair purchase.
mechanics.engine: Validate completed inventory and worker identity, then record an irreversible allocation. Prevent recall of quota commitments and later dispatch of retained workers. Payment is a separate contract rule still to design.
mechanics.carry: Every allocation changes the population or obligation permanently. Later output and risk develop from the factory actually retained.
mechanics.uiCost: A few totals and a focused allocation decision. Counts aggregate individuals without replacing them in the engine.

mechanics.name: Supervisor assignments and room fit
mechanics.stage: First playable slice, richer with each arrival
mechanics.see: Relevant expertise, observed track record, current commitments and attributed recommendations. Do not display hidden loyalty as an exact value.
mechanics.do: On day one, choose the adviser before any placements exist. Review and accept or override their initial arrangement. Later days use the previous roster as a baseline, but the adviser still selects the priority and proposes changes.
mechanics.engine: Room capability, prerequisites, personality and current BDI state shape eligible plans. State-grounded seeded variation resolves supported outcomes; good, poor and volatile fits differ.
mechanics.carry: Output and remembered treatment persist. An assignment can work technically while damaging respect or cooperation.
mechanics.uiCost: Put the adviser choice before the full room matrix. Show a few proposed changes and one expanded inspector; choosing a person and evaluating their proposal must be understandable without searching all placements.

mechanics.name: Stress, faults and accidents
mechanics.stage: First playable slice, expanded recovery later
mechanics.see: Overload, repeated hesitation, fault warnings, observed damage and who was present. Exact worker stress remains hidden in Act 1.
mechanics.do: In Parts 01–02, reduce further exposure or accept risk and handle incident disclosures and relationship responses. Only from Part 03 can an engineer be assigned to restore equipment; stopping alone is not repair.
mechanics.engine: Accumulate individual and equipment exposure. Resolve bounded severity from state and recorded randomness; identify witnesses; change worker/supervisor stress, confidence, capacity and memories.
mechanics.carry: Repeated incidents alter both physical viability and the credibility of later orders. Prevention preserves a real alternate path.
mechanics.uiCost: A few observable symptoms and one consequential incident surface; many individual updates need no separate alert.

mechanics.name: Daily advice and supervisor agency
mechanics.stage: First playable slice with minimal BDI
mechanics.see: The paused factory console shows opening facts and the weekly quota alongside the first adviser choice; later days show yesterday’s hard facts. Briefings separate assessment and attributed context from those facts, including any informed claim about worker conditioning.
mechanics.do: Choose one adviser for the day. Hear their judgment, ask permitted follow-ups and accept or override placements. During the shift, their own room resolves automatically; accept or override their proposals elsewhere. The player cannot supply a priority to the adviser.
mechanics.engine: BDI and current knowledge determine the adviser’s priority, plan and response proposals. Bind automatic authority to the adviser’s effective room assignment. Apply accepted or overridden responses through the local actor’s own agency; record each supervisor’s informed interpretation and effects on respect, loyalty and confidence. Prose expresses recorded decisions and permitted claims without changing direct facts.
mechanics.carry: Adviser choice, accepted decisions, overrides and differing reactions persist. Early sincere guidance teaches the system; later motives and stored hidden history support uncertainty and eventual revelation.
mechanics.uiCost: A primary daily choice, a concise briefing and clear automatic-versus-player decision status. The player learns why whom they choose matters; social costs and actual execution remain visible through consequences.

mechanics.name: Supervisor conflicts and development
mechanics.stage: Pair conflict from the start; modifications are later candidates
mechanics.see: Clashes over work, cooperation or refusal, remembered public decisions and changing behaviour. Pair relationships need not appear as numerical meters.
mechanics.do: Back an authority boundary, assign people whose methods can coexist, or address a specific breach in consultation. Training Limen or modifying a supervisor are possible side routes to design, not generic upgrades.
mechanics.engine: Track directed relationships, witnessed treatment and incompatible commitments. Resolve encounters through each actor’s knowledge and available plans. A supported training or modification changes specific capabilities or constraints rather than erasing personality and history.
mechanics.carry: An ally can become a rival; a protective intervention can later motivate cooperation or blame. Capability growth can change room fit and the balance of authority.
mechanics.uiCost: Use the existing assignment, report and consultation surfaces. Introduce a special intervention only when it creates a distinct, consequential choice.

mechanics.name: Disclosure, rumours and conflicting accounts
mechanics.stage: First slice uses direct claims and responses; richer propagation can follow
mechanics.see: Attributed reports and permitted evidence; differing accounts can conflict without the UI silently selecting the true one.
mechanics.do: Choose recipients and framing where an information decision is available; investigate or use the daily consultation to challenge an account.
mechanics.engine: Distinguish the physical event from claims about it. Track source, contacts, exposure, belief, rejection and relay. Failed rumour attempts need no global morale effect.
mechanics.carry: A supervisor’s account and the player’s response can affect later advice and cooperation. Multi-hop source comparison is deferred beyond the first playable.
mechanics.uiCost: One incident thread can represent many recipients. Never expose the full rumour graph in Act 1 by default.

mechanics.name: Cathexis and the Burn-in Theatre
mechanics.see: Programme, attendance, slogans and changed behaviour; Cathexis’s growing audience becomes visible through action.
mechanics.do: Choose programme and authority, make a commitment or pursue a designed constraint/side route. Conveyor assignment, compliance modification and revolutionary direction require their own consequences.
mechanics.engine: Record actual programme participation and its effects on beliefs, respect and allegiance. Workers produced before Theatre opening remain unindoctrinated until actual participation changes that history. Keep Cathexis’s loyalty and confidence separate. Reassignment cannot clear history; exact programme coverage and commitment branches remain open.
mechanics.carry: Coordination can improve while independent authority grows. The chosen fork brings a downstream liability that conversation cannot indefinitely cancel.
mechanics.uiCost: Introduce one programme decision family, not a screen for every belief. The audience’s behaviour carries much of the feedback.

mechanics.name: Rivet Witch and the Brewery
mechanics.see: Witch’s arrival introduces substrate production and engineering. Existing room damage now becomes actionable, with competing requests for her time.
mechanics.do: Fund and staff the function; prioritize technical repair versus current output and decide how much discretion to grant Witch.
mechanics.engine: Route Conveyor waste into substrate under the production recipe. For repairs, require engineering capability and reserve Witch’s time; resolve downtime and actual restoration without simultaneous incompatible Brewery work. Record reactions to neglected or completed faults. Cash alone cannot grant repair capability.
mechanics.carry: New production depends on the earlier line and its backlog. A useful repair can become an authority dispute.
mechanics.uiCost: Add one material flow when it becomes usable; summarize its source and destination rather than introducing a general inventory game.

mechanics.name: Thrum, Weaving and relief
mechanics.see: Precision work, changed worker behaviour after relief, lower productive attention and other supervisors’ objections.
mechanics.do: Allocate Thrum’s time between advanced production, preparation and available relief actions; accept the output/discipline cost explicitly.
mechanics.engine: Update worker stress, productive time and discipline through distinct effects. Thrum’s room fit and other supervisors’ interpretations affect future plans. Relief is not an all-purpose mental reset.
mechanics.carry: A healthier workforce may be harder to discipline. Other supervisors can oppose a beneficial intervention for understandable reasons.
mechanics.uiCost: A contextual allocation or programme choice; detailed individual relief histories remain underneath.

mechanics.name: Brain 1.5 and smart workers
mechanics.stage: Advanced chain produces a new output
mechanics.see: A completed advanced batch and the opportunity cost of selling versus retaining specialist workers.
mechanics.do: Commission the first batch, then allocate valuable output to income or internal capability.
mechanics.engine: Resolve Brewery/Weaving prerequisites and throughput; allow first production without an already-smart workforce. Preserve identities and histories if upgrades become a supported path.
mechanics.carry: Changed workforce composition affects production and social comparison. New capacity opens further investment choices.
mechanics.uiCost: Extend the existing allocation surface with a new category; do not create a second unrelated economy UI.

mechanics.name: Replacement rumours and scapegoating
mechanics.see: A report about incoming supervisors, allegations and the evidence the director can access. Distinguish reported performance from actual production records.
mechanics.do: Set or withhold assurances, investigate and eventually choose replacement policy. The rumour does not automatically fire the lowest performers.
mechanics.engine: Propagate knowledge of the threat through relationships. Self-protection, blame, loyalty and confidence affect intentions and selective reports; record actual contribution independently.
mechanics.carry: Old overrides, accident accounts and promises acquire new stakes. Two incoming supervisors change the authority structure in Act 2.
mechanics.uiCost: Reuse report and consultation surfaces with higher stakes; no new suspicion meter is required.

mechanics.name: Cortex Assembly and Brain 2.0
mechanics.stage: Act transition; beyond the first session
mechanics.see: A funded, functioning prototype project. Its purpose is not disclosed to the player at first-shift entry. Thought access later reveals existing histories under a defined knowledge policy.
mechanics.do: Invest and complete the chain; later use newly available inspection and social interventions.
mechanics.engine: Track prerequisites, progress and the actual population throughout Act 1. Completion grants specified capabilities and projections; it does not generate past beliefs on demand.
mechanics.carry: The exact workforce, damage, authority and secrets enter Act 2. Interpretation may remain imperfect even with access to thoughts.
mechanics.uiCost: New depth within the same inspector can reveal much more engine state without replacing the interface.

mechanics.name: First-floor autonomy and the second floor
mechanics.see: A compact operating summary, the current mandate and exceptions that require intervention.
mechanics.do: Set delegation boundaries and respond to material exceptions while managing the new floor and incoming supervisors.
mechanics.engine: Continue first-floor work, maintenance, information and relationships. Earned policies govern routine choices; nothing freezes merely because its view is collapsed.
mechanics.carry: Old dependencies and people can still create consequences upstairs. Incoming supervisor roster and endgame remain open.
mechanics.uiCost: More world activity can coincide with fewer routine controls. Delegation reduces attention demand, not simulation depth.

mechanics.name: Failure, recovery and episode traces
mechanics.see: Damage and actionable warning before terminal loss; afterward, a concise account tied to observed events and decisions.
mechanics.do: Choose a costly recovery while one exists; inspect permitted causes, resume or end a failed run explicitly.
mechanics.engine: Evaluate viability and recovery options; persist causal event links, commands, interpretation/admission records and seeded outcomes. Select matching art and recaps from events rather than forcing events to fit art.
